messages:
noah: Heads up — we've been seeing elevated inter-region packet loss from us-west1 -> us-east1 for the last 3 hours. CPU on scheduler looks fine, but several GPU pods failed handshakes and got punted to local pools.
priya: I can see the same in the net metrics. 15-25% retransmits on the overlay during peak window (18:00-20:30 UTC). Could explain why bin-packing is ending up more fragmented — jobs prefer local nodes.
alex: Any spike in small-multipod jobs? Fragmentation + network blips = long tail preemptions.
priya: Yep — commerce customers ramped traffic. Small 2-4 GPU jobs increased ~40% vs baseline. They trigger our small-slot placement which tries cross-pool packing sometimes — that interacts poorly with packet loss.
jamie: infra-bot flagged a +18% increase in eviction events in the last 2h. infra-bot: [ALERT] eviction-rate(us-west1): +18% | packet-drop: 19% | affected-pools: gpu-small-*, gpu-shared-2
noah: Short term: we should stop cross-region bursting for small jobs and force strict region-local placement until link stabilizes. Agree?
alex: Agreed. Policy change: set "region_affinity: strict" for job size <=4 GPUs and for classes A/B. That'll increase cost a bit but reduce preempt churn.
priya: Also propose we flip scheduling preference to prefer bandwidth-healthy NICs. Add a network-health penalty to the scoring function: score -= 1000 * packet_loss_pct for region mismatch.
jamie: That sounds safe. We need a canary though. Maybe apply to 10% of small jobs first.
noah: Good call. 10% canary starting in 10m. If eviction rate drops and latency returns to normal, roll to 100% after 2h.
sre-oncall: SRE note: we'll hold off automated defrag compaction until link recovers. Defrag will cause extra cross-host traffic and could worsen packet loss.
alex: Long term: we should teach the bin-packer cost model about net egress cost + expected retransmit tax. Right now it only considers GPU hours and memory fit.
priya: Agreed. We can add a network-weighted cost term and an optional "latency-safe" relaxation: for latency-sensitive jobs we prioritize co-location even if packing is slightly worse.
jamie: Can we measure the unit cost of retransmits? Ballpark egress ops and wasted compute due to replays — need a model for cost tradeoffs.
noah: I'll sketch a simple estimator: wasted_gpu_seconds = evicted_jobs * avg_run_duration * fraction_wasted; network_penalty = wasted_gpu_seconds * gpu_hour_cost + retransmit_bytes * egress_cost.
priya: Throwing numbers: in last 3h, evicted_jobs ~ 120, avg_run_duration 900s, fraction_wasted 0.6 -> wasted_gpu_seconds ~ 64,800s ~ 18 GPU-hours. At $3/hr that's ~$54 + egress. Not huge but multiplied by frequent events it adds up.
jamie: Ok actionable list: 1) Apply region_affinity strict for <=4 GPU jobs (canary 10%). 2) Add network-health penalty in scoring (canary). 3) Pause defrag jobs for 4h. 4) Run a targeted evict/repack dry-run in staging with synthetic packet loss to validate scheduler changes.
noah: I'll open the rollout PR for policy flip and canary flags. @alex can you prototype scoring change? @sre-oncall please coordinate monitoring thresholds and PagerDuty mute for defrag alerts.
alex: On it — will push a branch with a simple linear penalty and unit tests.
sre-oncall: Mute set for defrag alerts for 4h. We'll keep pager fatigue low.
priya: Also let's add a small dashboard tile: "inter-region packet loss vs eviction-rate" so PMs can see correlation quickly.
jamie: If we hold packets high for >6h we should consider pre-warming extra local capacity for high-volume tenants to avoid repeated churn. Might be an op-ex/contract discussion.
noah: Agree. For now actioning the canary and monitoring. I'll post updates in 30m. :white_check_mark:
alex: Quick snippet for the scoring change (in-thread):
```
// pseudo
score = base_fit_score - (packet_loss_pct * NET_PENALTY_FACTOR) - (egress_bytes_gb * EGRESS_COST_WEIGHT)
```
Keep NET_PENALTY_FACTOR small initially (0.01).
priya: Thanks. If canary shows >30% reduction in evictions we roll immediately.
noah: Thanks everyone. I'll file the PR and link it here.
noah: PR: https://internal.git/repo/infra/scheduler/pulls/412 (WIP)
jamie: Land the canary flag behind experiments toggle so we can ramp back if needed.
infra-bot: [DEPLOY] scheduler-canary applied to 10% traffic in us-west1 at 2052509901
noah: Canary started. Monitoring: eviction-rate, packet-loss, scheduling-latency. I'll report in 30m.
priya: Seeing immediate drop in cross-host reconnections for canary cohort. Preliminary good sign. :thumbsup:
